catalog_quote: [Madan 1908 p.11] The accent in Lala and Wisa is usually on the syllable before the last, but a stress is also very commonly laid on the last syllable but two. [Madan 1906 p.9 sec.10] The Wisa accent must be learnt by ear, and cannot as yet be reduced to rule. In Bantu dialects the accent commonly falls on the last syllable but one. In Wisa, a stress is very often heard on the last syllable but two, even when an unimportant one. The effect of this, however, appears to be to lighten rather than to remove the usual accent on the syllable following ... [Kashoki & Mann 1978 pp.70-71, sec. 3.4] In Zambian languages, in contrast, syllables are more or less evenly stressed, i.e. they are pronounced with almost the same degree of prominence or force. ... audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes on all three held files at the stated locators. The coding (tonal, no word-stress rule; impressionistic penult accent with frequent antepenult stress as secondary) rests on two 1906/1908 missionary handbooks plus a 1978 Zambia-wide survey chapter that presents no Lala-Bisa data, so the evidence is old and partly second-hand, but nothing located contradicts it: Glottolog (MED = Madan 1906; 57 language refs, 105 family-node refs), Grambank (source = Madan 1906), the UNZA repository and Semantic Scholar show no grammar, phonology, tone or instrumental study of Lala-Bisa. No open source could be fetched sources (search engines blocked, budgets exhausted; one Wayback PDF turned out to be a mislinked unrelated article and was discarded). The only modern prosodic analysis nearby is Bickmore 1995 on Lamba, a distinct sister languoid, which could inform but not recode this record. Henc

sources.note: Closest sister language in the same Bisa-Lamba (M.50) node (Madan 1908 itself treats 'Lala-Lamba' as one handbook); an explicit formal analysis of stress-tone interaction that tests whether Kashoki & Mann's areal 'evenly stressed, two tones' claim, on which our coding rests, holds for the M.50 group. Comparative only; cannot recode lala1264 by itself.
